description: Universal Production with Ported Gothic Aesthetics
anchor_block: hyper-realistic gothic horror animation, Victorian archive interior, central antique gold-framed mirror with cracked glass in mid-frame, flickering amber lantern left-frame, leather-bound books and aged scrolls foreground, low-angle upward camera perspective, blue-gray atmospheric mist and dust motes in the air, deep crimson accent lighting, Tim Burton cinematic style, shallow depth of field, no on-screen text, no people in modern clothing
visual_prompts: A dark Victorian archive at night, an enormous antique mirror on the wall begins to ripple like water
Ancient parchment documents and royal seals on a desk, a portrait of Queen Mary I glowing with amber light
A quill pen writing 'MARY' in blood-red ink on a document that is slowly turning to ash
The central mirror begins to crack in a web-like pattern, crimson light leaking from the fissures
Extreme close-up on the mirror as a pale hand presses against the glass from the inside
A cloaked figure desperately stacking heavy books over a glowing document that is bleeding shadows
The archive room plunging into darkness as the final lantern goes out, mirror glowing in deep crimson

scenes.text: What if Bloody Mary was not a myth... but a royal cover-up buried for five centuries?
Queen Mary the First. 1553. She burned nearly three hundred people alive.
History called her mad. But the documents tell a different story...
She wasn't mad. She was trying to communicate with something on the other side.
And it answered. With a reflection that didn't belong to her.
The church knew. The crown knew. And they moved quickly to make sure you never would.
But one record survived. And tonight... it surfaced in this room. Watch the shadows.
